docs.title: Superluminal API Documentation
docs.text: Use the Superluminal API to consume market data, authenticate a Fogo wallet, fund trading subaccounts, and submit signed trading commands.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• C++ client: build and run the reference C++ client.
  • Python client: install and run the Python SDK and TUI.
  • Fund an account: use the public testnet faucet or prepare an address for a manual collateral transfer.
  • Public API: HTTP and WebSocket requests, responses, pagination, and rejection reasons.

docs.title: Account identity
docs.text:
Your Fogo Ed25519 wallet public key identifies your Superluminal account. Each wallet can own multiple numbered trading subaccounts. Authentication proves control of the wallet; signed commands identify the target subaccount.

Fund the wallet before starting a trading client. The public gateway permits one authenticated WebSocket session per wallet, so a newer session preempts an older one.

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text:
• Max inbound frame size: 256 KiB
  • Max inbound text command size: 64 KiB
  • Max signed proof payload size: 512 bytes
  • Per-connection inbound WebSocket message rate limit, including data frames and ping/pong control frames:
  • 3000 messages/minute
  • burst capacity of 150 messages
  • exceeded connections are closed with msg_rate_limit_exceeded
  • order-like commands are counted by this same limiter:
    • signed_order
    • signed_cancel
    • signed_modify
    • signed_conditional_group
    • signed_conditional_cancel
  • deposit/withdraw commands are also counted by this same limiter.
  • application-level ping messages and WebSocket ping/pong control frames are counted by this same limiter.
  • invalid or unauthenticated messages are counted before command validation so malformed-message floods cannot bypass the limit.
  • The burst capacity allows brief traffic above the per-minute refill rate; clients must then wait for capacity to refill.
  • Ping/pong:
  • Server sends ping every 20s.
  • Read deadline is 120s and extended on pong.

docs.title: Origin policy
docs.text:
• Browser connections are checked against the deployment's origin allowlist at WebSocket upgrade.
  • Non-browser API clients may omit the Origin header.

docs.title: GET /v1/symbology
docs.text:
Returns a symbology snapshot.

Sample response:

{
  "version": 123,
  "taker_fee_ppm": 100,
  "maker_fee_ppm": -10,
  "markets": [
    {
      "id": 7,
      "symbol": "BTC",
      "quote": "USDC",
      "pyth_feed_id": 1,
      "max_funding_rate_e8": 10000,
      "px_exponent": -8,
      "tick_size": 100,
      "size_decimals": 5,
      "initial_margin_bps": 500,
      "maintenance_margin_bps": 250,
      "transfer_margin_floor_bps": 1000,
      "status": "active"
    }
  ]
}

Each market includes required metadata:

  • quote
  • pyth_feed_id
  • max_funding_rate_e8
  • px_exponent
  • tick_size
  • size_decimals
  • initial_margin_bps
  • maintenance_margin_bps
  • transfer_margin_floor_bps

Top-level taker_fee_ppm and maker_fee_ppm are present when exchange config is loaded; otherwise they default to 0.

docs.title: GET /v1/evm/addresses
docs.text:
Returns public EVM deployment metadata needed by clients to compute user deposit addresses and submit EVM token transfers.

Sample response:

{
  "version": 1,
  "collateral": "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
  "gateway": "0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222",
  "fee_recipient": "0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333",
  "user_deposit_init_code_hash": "0x4444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444"
}

Fields:

  • version: response schema version.
  • collateral: ERC20 collateral token address on the EVM chain.
  • gateway: deployed EVMVault address on the EVM chain.
  • fee_recipient: EVM fee recipient address.
  • user_deposit_init_code_hash: CREATE2 init code hash for UserDeposit.

Status:

  • 200: EVM address metadata is configured.
  • 503: gateway has no EVM address metadata configured.

docs.title: Hyperliquid Compatibility
docs.text:
The gateway exposes a small, public market-data surface intended to be Hyperliquid-compatible.

For lowest latency, clients should prefer the native subscribe_market market-data API over the Hyperliquid compatibility layer. The native stream forwards raw gateway market data without the extra channel wrapping, filtering, and format conversion used by the HL-compatible channels.

Maker/taker behavior:

  • Native subscribe_market exposes raw public book events for both maker and taker books.
  • Raw BookSnapshot, BookDelta, and stream_reset book events are tagged with bookType.
  • Hyperliquid-compatible derived book channels are maker-only:
  • l2Book is built from the maker book only.
  • bbo is built from the maker book only.
  • allMids is computed from maker-book BBOs only.
  • If a client needs taker-book data, it must use the native raw subscribe_market stream and filter by bookType: "taker".

Supported HL-compatible endpoints:

  • POST /info with {"type":"meta"}
  • WebSocket subscribe / unsubscribe for:
  • l2Book
  • bbo
  • trades
  • allMids

This compatibility surface is market-data only. Authentication, private account streaming, and signed order entry use the native Superluminal API.

docs.title: HL WebSocket subscription ack shape
docs.text:
Successful HL-style subscribe commands return:

{
  "channel": "subscriptionResponse",
  "data": {
    "method": "subscribe",
    "subscription": {
      "type": "trades",
      "coin": "BTC"
    }
  }
}

Notes:

  • The response uses a nested data.subscription object.
  • The subscription object reflects the normalized subscription accepted by the gateway.
  • HL-style unsubscribe does not emit an ack; the gateway just stops delivering that channel.

docs.title: WebSocket API
docs.text:
Default URL: ws://<public-host>:<public-port>/ws

Inbound WS commands use one of two shapes:

  • Superluminal-native commands with a required type field
  • Hyperliquid-style market-data commands with method and subscription Unknown fields are rejected for command payloads.

• ack

  • Public market stream events (for example BookSnapshot, BookDelta, Trade, FundingIndex, stream_reset)
  • Hyperliquid-style channel-wrapped public market events (subscriptionResponse, l2Book, bbo, trades, allMids)
  • Private/account events (for example AccountSnapshot, Fill, FillSettled, FillBusted, OrderAccepted, CancelAck, ModifyAck, ModifyReject, UserDepositAddressStatus, UserCollateralUpdate, AccountFundingUpdate, LiquidationTriggered, LiquidationCleared)

Notes:

  • Streamed matching events include matcher_unix_ns.
  • Streamed events routed through gateway include gateway_send_unix_ns.
  • Private Fill events include execution_mode with the signed-order values:
  • 0 = NORMAL
  • 1 = MAINTENANCE_LIQUIDATION
  • 2 = ADL
  • 3 = VAULT_LIQUIDATION

docs.title: Auth gating
docs.text:
• Unauthenticated clients can only use public market data commands (subscribe_market, Hyperliquid-style l2Book / bbo / trades / allMids subscribe/unsubscribe, ping).
  • Private/account actions and signed submit require authentication.

docs.title: Auth mode
docs.text: Each WS connection authenticates with wallet challenge mode: auth_wallet -> auth_response.

docs.title: Exactly 1 active authenticated WS per wallet
docs.text:
This gateway enforces one active authenticated WS per bound wallet.

What this means:

  • If a new connection authenticates/binds the same wallet, the previous connection is preempted.
  • The old connection receives:
{
  "type": "session_preempted",
  "reason": "new_session_authenticated"
}
  • Then old connection auth state is cleared and socket is disconnected.

Concrete examples:

  • API bot has wallet W authenticated/bound on WS-1. The same wallet authenticates on WS-2: WS-1 gets session_preempted and disconnects.

docs.title: subscribe_market (public)
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "subscribe_market", "symbol": 7 }

Fields:

  • type: literal string subscribe_market
  • symbol: active symbology market id (uint32 on the wire; for example 7)

Success:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "accepted" }

Failure example:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "rejected", "reason": "invalid_symbol" }

Streaming behavior:

  • subscribe_market is the native public raw market-data stream.
  • Raw BookSnapshot, BookDelta, and Trade payloads include the stream sequence in seq.
  • Raw BookSnapshot and BookDelta payloads on this stream carry bookType: "maker" or bookType: "taker".
  • Clients should filter book events by bookType if they only want one view.
  • Raw Trade events remain on this stream.
  • Raw FundingIndex events are also delivered on this stream when funding index updates are published for a subscribed market.
  • stream_reset payloads for this stream also carry bookType, and unfiltered recovery may emit one reset for maker and one for taker.

Native BookSnapshot example:

{
  "type": "BookSnapshot",
  "seq": 101,
  "bookType": "maker",
  "id": 7,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "book_cursor": 5000,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1710000000000000000,
  "depth_cap": 100,
  "bids": [
    { "price": 10001000000, "qty": 500000, "order_count": 1 }
  ],
  "asks": [
    { "price": 10002000000, "qty": 300000, "order_count": 2 }
  ],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000000100000
}

Native BookDelta example:

{
  "type": "BookDelta",
  "seq": 102,
  "bookType": "maker",
  "id": 7,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "prev_book_cursor": 5000,
  "book_cursor": 5001,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1710000000001000000,
  "depth_cap": 100,
  "mark_price": 10001500000,
  "bids": [
    { "price": 10001000000, "qty": 700000, "order_count": 2 }
  ],
  "asks": [
    { "price": 10002000000, "qty": 0, "order_count": 0 }
  ],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000001100000
}

Native Trade example:

{
  "type": "Trade",
  "seq": 103,
  "id": 7,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1710000000002000000,
  "trade_id": 77,
  "side": "B",
  "price": 10001500000,
  "qty": 200000,
  "hash": "0",
  "buyer": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "seller": [5, 6, 7, 8],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000002100000
}

Native FundingIndex example:

{
  "type": "FundingIndex",
  "seq": 104,
  "oracle_price_batch_id": 44,
  "entries": [
    {
      "market_id": 7,
      "perp_price": 10001500000,
      "premium_e8": 250,
      "cum_funding_index_e8": 123456
    }
  ],
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1710000000003100000
}

Notes:

  • price, qty, mark_price, and perp_price are raw integer values interpreted using the market's symbology metadata.
  • premium_e8 and cum_funding_index_e8 are signed fixed-point values scaled by 1e8.
  • Optional fields such as seq, batch_id, term, depth_cap, and truncated are omitted when they have zero or false values.
  • gateway_send_unix_ns is added by the gateway immediately before sending the event to the client.

docs.title: Hyperliquid-style l2Book subscribe (public)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "method": "subscribe",
  "subscription": { "type": "l2Book", "coin": "BTC" }
}

Supported subscription fields:

  • type: must be l2Book
  • coin: active market symbol string from symbology, for example BTC
  • nSigFigs: optional, supported values are 2, 3, 4, 5
  • mantissa: optional, only valid when nSigFigs is 5; supported values are 2 or 5

Success response:

{
  "channel": "subscriptionResponse",
  "data": {
    "method": "subscribe",
    "subscription": { "type": "l2Book", "coin": "BTC" }
  }
}

Streaming payloads:

{
  "channel": "l2Book",
  "data": {
    "coin": "BTC",
    "levels": [
      [{"px":"100.01","sz":"5","n":1}],
      [{"px":"100.02","sz":"3","n":2}]
    ],
    "time": 1710000000000
  }
}

Notes:

  • This is additive; it does not replace subscribe_market.
  • Client-facing l2Book payloads follow the Hyperliquid shape.
  • l2Book is derived from the maker book only; the taker book is not exposed on this HL-compatible channel.

docs.title: Native candle commands (public)
docs.text:
Supported candle resolutions:

  • Canonical names: 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 1d, 1w
  • Accepted aliases: 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 240, D, 1D, daily, W, 1W, weekly
  • Missing or empty resolution is accepted as 1m.

The canonical candle resolution is 1m. Higher resolutions are derived from finalized 1m candles.

Requests identify markets with market_id. For legacy clients, if market_id is omitted or 0, the numeric symbol field is used as the market id. Prefer market_id in new clients. Response symbol fields are display symbols such as BTC.

Range request:

{
  "type": "get_candle_range",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "1h"
}

Range response:

{
  "type": "candle_range",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "1h",
  "available": true,
  "oldest_time_unix_s": 1700002800,
  "latest_time_unix_s": 1707685200
}

For derived resolutions, oldest_time_unix_s and latest_time_unix_s are fully complete bucket starts. In-progress derived buckets are not advertised by candle_range. For 1m, all published source candles are already final.

If no candles are available, the response is:

{
  "type": "candle_range",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "1m",
  "available": false
}

Historical request:

{
  "type": "get_candles",
  "request_id": "chart-1",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "5m",
  "from_unix_s": 1707684000,
  "to_unix_s": 1707687600,
  "limit": 500
}

get_candles fields:

  • from_unix_s and to_unix_s are required, nonzero Unix seconds. from_unix_s must be less than to_unix_s.
  • The range is half-open: [from_unix_s, to_unix_s).
  • limit is optional. 0 or an omitted value uses the default 5000. The maximum accepted limit is 10000.
  • Candles are returned in ascending time_unix_s order.

Historical response:

{
  "type": "candles",
  "request_id": "chart-1",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "5m",
  "from_unix_s": 1707684000,
  "to_unix_s": 1707687600,
  "available": true,
  "partial": false,
  "candles": [
    {
      "time_unix_s": 1707684000,
      "symbol": "BTC",
      "open": 1000000,
      "high": 1010000,
      "low": 990000,
      "close": 1005000,
      "volume": 250000,
      "trade_count": 42,
      "first_trade_id": 100,
      "last_trade_id": 141,
      "first_trade_unix_ns": 1707684000123456789,
      "last_trade_unix_ns": 1707684059123456789,
      "source_market_data_seq": 12345,
      "is_final": true
    }
  ]
}

get_candles may include the current in-progress derived bucket when the requested range reaches the latest available data; that candle has is_final: false.

If no candles are available, the gateway returns a candles event with available: false, partial: false, and an empty candles array. reason may be present:

  • stream_unavailable: no retained candle stream is available for the requested market.
  • history_unavailable: historical candles are temporarily unavailable.

partial: true means the returned set is incomplete. This can happen when the response is truncated by limit or only part of the requested range is temporarily available.

Per-candle optional fields:

  • symbol: present when known.
  • first_trade_id, last_trade_id, first_trade_unix_ns, last_trade_unix_ns: omitted when the candle has no trades or the source did not provide those values.

Live subscribe:

{
  "type": "subscribe_candles",
  "market_id": 1,
  "resolution": "5m"
}

Live candle event:

{
  "type": "candle",
  "market_id": 1,
  "symbol": "BTC",
  "resolution": "5m",
  "seq": 100,
  "app_seq": 100,
  "time_unix_s": 1707684000,
  "open": 1000000,
  "high": 1010000,
  "low": 990000,
  "close": 1005000,
  "volume": 250000,
  "trade_count": 42,
  "first_trade_id": 100,
  "last_trade_id": 141,
  "first_trade_unix_ns": 1707684000123456789,
  "last_trade_unix_ns": 1707684059123456789,
  "source_market_data_seq": 12345,
  "is_final": false
}

For derived live subscriptions, updates have is_final: false while the derived bucket is open. A final update with is_final: true is emitted when the bucket completes. unsubscribe_candles uses the same market_id and resolution fields.

Candle command rejects use the normal ack rejection shape:

  • invalid_candle_subscription: request JSON is malformed or contains unknown fields.
  • invalid_resolution: resolution is not one of the supported values above.
  • invalid_symbol: the requested market id is not active.
  • invalid_candle_range: get_candles has missing/zero bounds or from_unix_s >= to_unix_s.
  • candle_limit_too_large: get_candles.limit > 10000.

docs.title: auth_wallet (start wallet challenge)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "auth_wallet",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<base58>",
  "expiry_seconds": 300
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string auth_wallet
  • wallet_pubkey: required Solana public key in base58
  • expiry_seconds: required integer; 0 means never expire, otherwise must be > 60

Rules:

  • expiry_seconds is required.
  • expiry_seconds = 0 means the wallet-auth session does not expire by gateway TTL.
  • Positive expiry_seconds values must be > 60.
  • wallet_pubkey is required.
  • This is the only command that issues wallet challenges.

On success:

  • auth_challenge event
  • then ack accepted

The challenge is sent before the accepted ack on the WebSocket.

{
  "type": "auth_challenge",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<wallet>",
  "nonce": "<nonce>",
  "issued_unix_ms": 1710000000000,
  "expires_unix_ms": 1710000060000,
  "session_id": "<gateway_session_id>",
  "message": "AETHON_AUTH_V1|<wallet_pubkey>|<nonce>|<iat>|<exp>|<session_id>"
}

docs.title: auth_response (complete wallet challenge)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "auth_response",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<optional wallet pubkey>",
  "nonce": "<challenge nonce>",
  "signature_b64": "<ed25519 signature over challenge message bytes>",
  "signed_payload_b64": "<optional Ledger V0 signed payload bytes>",
  "is_delegate": true
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string auth_response
  • wallet_pubkey: optional base58 pubkey; if supplied it must match the challenged wallet
  • nonce: exact nonce from auth_challenge
  • signature_b64: base64-encoded ed25519 signature over the exact auth_challenge.message bytes
  • signed_payload_b64: optional base64-encoded Solana off-chain V0 signed payload. When present, the Ledger prefix and body are verified and the signature is checked over the full signed payload.
  • is_delegate: optional boolean; when true, the signature must verify with the wallet's current delegate key

Rules:

  • Challenge TTL is 60s.
  • Challenge is single-use (replay rejected).
  • Without is_delegate, signature must verify against the challenged wallet pubkey and exact challenge message.
  • With is_delegate: true, the signature must verify with the challenged wallet's currently registered delegate key.
  • On success, wallet is automatically bound for signed-submit authorization.
  • Delegate-authenticated sessions may submit orders, cancels, modifies, vault operations, and subaccount transfers.
  • Collateral withdraw requires owner wallet authentication; delegate-authenticated sessions are rejected for signed_withdraw.

Delegate rotation warning:

  • Before changing a wallet's delegate key, cancel all open orders for that wallet.
  • Existing resting orders are not automatically canceled when the delegate changes.
  • Orders signed by a previous delegate may fail settlement after the delegate key is updated.

Success:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "accepted" }

docs.title: Ledger Hardware Wallet Signing
docs.text:
Ledger Solana hardware wallets sign Solana off-chain message payloads, not the raw gateway message bytes. Ledger clients should use Solana off-chain message V0 signing.

V0 signed payload layout:

0xff || "solana offchain" ||
version(1) ||
app_domain(32) ||
format(1) ||
signer_count(1) ||
signer_pubkey(32) ||
message_len_le_u16(2) ||
message_body

Gateway Ledger clients use:

version = 0
app_domain = "aethon-gateway" padded with zero bytes to 32 bytes
format = 0
signer_count = 1
signer_pubkey = wallet pubkey bytes

The V0 prefix before message_body is 85 bytes.

Auth challenge Ledger body:

AETHON_AUTH_V1|<wallet_pubkey>|<nonce>|<iat>|<exp>|<session_id>

This is the exact auth_challenge.message encoded as UTF-8.

signed_set_delegate Ledger body:

base64(owner_pubkey || delegate_key || delegate_nonce_le_u64 || request_id64_le_u64 || iat_le_u64 || exp_le_u64)

The base64 wrapper is used because the set-delegate payload contains binary bytes, while Ledger Solana off-chain V0 message bodies must be valid text.

docs.title: subscribe_account (private stream)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "subscribe_account"
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string subscribe_account
  • No other request fields are accepted.

Behavior:

  • Requires authentication.
  • Uses the wallet already bound by authentication state.
  • Does not mutate authentication state.
  • On success, starts private wallet stream and snapshot bootstrap.

Success:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "accepted" }

Then private events such as:

{
  "type": "AccountSnapshot",
  "wallet_pubkey": "<wallet>",
  "wallet": [1,2,3,4],
  "last_seq": 12345,
  "subaccounts": [{
    "subaccount_id": 0,
    "collateral_balance": 123456789,
    "accrued_fee": 4,
    "accrued_funding": -25,
    "status": "active",
    "positions": [{
      "symbol": 1,
      "net_qty": 10,
      "cost_basis": 1234560,
      "realized_pnl": 0,
      "funding_accrued": -25,
      "last_funding_index_e8": 1250,
      "pending_fees": 4
    }],
    "working_orders": [{
      "external_order_id": 123456,
      "client_instruction_id": 9001,
      "original_iat": 1710000000,
      "symbol": 1,
      "side": "BID",
      "role": "MAKER",
      "tif": "GTC",
      "order_type": 1,
      "price": 5000100,
      "original_qty": 2000,
      "remaining_qty": 2000,
      "delta_ppm": 0
    }]
  }],
  "vault_accounts": [{
    "vault_id": 0,
    "operation_subaccount_id": 1,
    "leader_source_subaccount_id": 0,
    "collateral_amount": 100000000000,
    "total_vault_shares": 100000000000,
    "last_seq": 12345
  }],
  "vault_participant_accounts": [{
    "participant_account_pubkey": "<pubkey>",
    "owner_wallet_pubkey": "<wallet>",
    "entry_count": 1,
    "last_seq": 12345,
    "entries": [{
      "vault_account_pubkey": "<pubkey>",
      "shares": 100000000000,
      "remaining_cost_basis": 100000000000,
      "last_seq": 12345
    }]
  }]
}

collateral_balance in AccountSnapshot and UserCollateralUpdate is the net user-visible collateral for that subaccount. It reflects the current collateral after fees and funding paid or accrued. AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].accrued_fee is the total accrued fee included in that net value, and AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].accrued_funding is the total accrued funding included in that net value.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].status is one of active, liquidating, or delinquent. A delinquent subaccount also includes owe_to_insurance with the current amount owed to insurance.

AccountSnapshot.subaccounts[].positions[].realized_pnl, funding_accrued, last_funding_index_e8, and pending_fees are emitted as numeric fields for every position. If a historical value is unavailable, the field is emitted as 0.

Private stream events are authoritative; signed submit commands do not emit an immediate success acknowledgement. Event types include:

  • Account bootstrap/errors: AccountSnapshot, AccountSnapshotError
  • Order lifecycle: OrderAccepted, ConditionalApproved, OrderReject, CancelAck, CancelReject, ModifyAck, ModifyReject
  • Fills and settlement: Fill, FillSettled, FillBusted
  • Collateral and funding: UserDepositAddressStatus, UserCollateralUpdate, AccountFundingUpdate
  • Liquidation status: LiquidationTriggered, LiquidationCleared
  • Withdraw settlement: WithdrawStatus
  • Vault and transfer settlement: CreateVaultStatus, CreateVault, DepositVaultStatus, DepositVault, WithdrawVaultStatus, WithdrawVault, TransferSubaccountStatus, SetDelegateStatus, VaultOperationSubaccountCollateralChange

String enum values in private account events use:

  • side: BID or ASK
  • role: MAKER or TAKER
  • tif: GTC or IOC

UserCollateralUpdate example:

{
  "type": "UserCollateralUpdate",
  "seq": 12346,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "collateral_delta": 1000000,
  "collateral_balance": 124456789,
  "fee": 0,
  "actual_deposit": 1000000,
  "total_deposit": 1000000,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000100000
}

UserDepositAddressStatus is emitted after deposit-address registration completes. It echoes the request timestamps for correlation:

{
  "type": "UserDepositAddressStatus",
  "seq": 12345,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "client_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000,
  "gateway_recv_unix_ns": 1735689600000001000,
  "sequencer_recv_unix_ns": 1735689600000002000,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000003000
}

OrderReject.reason is a numeric order-reject code. Risk rejections use these detailed codes:

  • 1 = MissingSymbology
  • 2 = Full
  • 3 = RiskRejected (legacy generic risk rejection)
  • 4 = RiskRejectedLiquidationNotActive — account is not liquidating
  • 5 = RiskRejectedSubaccountNotActive — account is inactive or liquidating
  • 6 = RiskRejectedInsufficientFreeCollateral — insufficient free collateral
  • 7 = ConditionalUnknownSubaccount
  • 8 = ConditionalUnknownPosition
  • 9 = ConditionalPositionDirection
  • 10 = ConditionalInsufficientCloseQuantity
  • 11 = ConditionalOpenOrders
  • 12 = ConditionalInvalidGroup
  • 13 = ConditionalFull
  • 14 = ConditionalMissingSymbology
  • 15 = ConditionalOwnerConflict

Clients should treat unknown numeric values as distinct reject reasons rather than coercing them to a generic error. Synchronous preflight rejections use a string reason instead (for example, "Permission Denied").

ConditionalApproved is emitted after Bop durably admits a conditional group. It identifies the group and each enabled dormant leg:

{
  "type": "ConditionalApproved",
  "seq": 12345,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "client_instruction_id": 9009,
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "side": "ASK",
  "group_external_order_id": 101,
  "take_profit_external_order_id": 99,
  "stop_loss_external_order_id": 100,
  "leg_flags": 3,
  "tp_trigger_sources": 3,
  "sl_trigger_sources": 2,
  "tp_trigger_price": 110,
  "tp_limit_price": 110,
  "sl_trigger_price": 90,
  "qty": 5,
  "expiry_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000
}

Subsequent fills and CancelAck events use the corresponding leg external order ID. When one OCO leg activates, Bop cancels the dormant sibling and submits the selected leg as a regular order for the next auction.

AccountFundingUpdate example:

{
  "type": "AccountFundingUpdate",
  "seq": 12347,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "symbol": 7,
  "market_id": 7,
  "prev_funding_index_e8": 1000,
  "last_funding_index_e8": 1250,
  "funding_delta": -25,
  "funding_accrued": -25,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000200000
}

LiquidationTriggered example:

{
  "type": "LiquidationTriggered",
  "seq": 12348,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "batch_id": 88,
  "account_status": "liquidating",
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000300000
}

LiquidationCleared example:

{
  "type": "LiquidationCleared",
  "seq": 12349,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "batch_id": 89,
  "account_status": "delinquent",
  "owe_to_insurance": 2500000,
  "gateway_send_unix_ns": 1735689600000400000
}

ModifyAck example:

{
  "type": "ModifyAck",
  "seq": 12346,
  "global_seq": 12346,
  "batch_id": 88,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000,
  "symbol": 7,
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "GTC",
  "order_type": 1,
  "client_instruction_id": 9005,
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "client_unix_ns": 1735689599999000000,
  "gateway_recv_unix_ns": 1735689599999500000,
  "sequencer_recv_unix_ns": 1735689599999700000,
  "price": 5000100,
  "qty": 2000,
  "delta_ppm": 25,
  "execution_mode": 0
}

ModifyReject has the same order identity fields plus reason; price, qty, and delta_ppm are the rejected requested values when present:

{
  "type": "ModifyReject",
  "seq": 12347,
  "global_seq": 12347,
  "batch_id": 88,
  "matcher_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000,
  "symbol": 7,
  "side": "BID",
  "role": "MAKER",
  "tif": "GTC",
  "order_type": 1,
  "client_instruction_id": 9006,
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "reason": 2,
  "price": 5000200,
  "qty": 2000,
  "delta_ppm": 30
}

Modify reject reason codes:

  • 1 = UnknownOrder
  • 2 = RoleMismatch
  • 3 = IOCNotModifiable
  • 4 = MarketNotModifiable
  • 5 = InvalidQty
  • 6 = InvalidPrice
  • 7 = Full
  • 8 = MissingSymbology

docs.title: get_order_history (private, paginated)
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "get_order_history",
  "request_id": "hist-1",
  "created_from_unix_s": 1735689600,
  "created_to_unix_s": 1738368000,
  "cursor": "",
  "limit": 20
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string get_order_history
  • request_id: optional caller-supplied correlation id; echoed back in the response so multiple in-flight pages can be matched up
  • created_from_unix_s: optional inclusive lower bound on order creation time, as UTC Unix seconds
  • created_to_unix_s: optional exclusive upper bound on order creation time, as UTC Unix seconds
  • cursor: optional opaque string from the previous page's next_cursor; empty or omitted returns the newest page
  • limit: optional page size; clamped to 1..100, defaults to 20

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated wallet-bound session (same gating as subscribe_account).
  • Orders are returned for the authenticated bound wallet only; the request does not accept a wallet override.
  • Creation-time filtering uses the half-open interval [created_from_unix_s, created_to_unix_s). Either bound may be omitted for an open-ended query. Supplied bounds must be non-negative integers, and created_from_unix_s must be less than created_to_unix_s when both are present. JSON null is invalid; omit an unused bound instead.
  • next_cursor binds the first page's creation-time bounds. Later pages may omit the bounds and use the cursor alone. If either bound is supplied with a cursor, it must match the bound encoded in that cursor.
  • Strict JSON: unknown fields are rejected with invalid_get_order_history.

Response (one order_history event per request, then ack accepted):

{
  "type": "order_history",
  "request_id": "hist-1",
  "next_cursor": "AgAAAAAAADA-AAAAAAAAMD4AAAAAAAHiQAAAAAcDAAAAAGd0hYAAAAAAZ51kAA",
  "orders": [
    {
      "external_order_id": 123456,
      "client_instruction_id": 9001,
      "subaccount_id": 0,
      "symbol": 7,
      "side": "BID",
      "role": "TAKER",
      "tif": "GTC",
      "order_type": 0,
      "status": "filled",
      "original_iat": 1735689600,
      "created_unix_ns": 1735689600123456789,
      "closed_unix_ns": 1735689601000000000,
      "price": 5000100,
      "original_qty": 2000,
      "remaining_qty": 0,
      "filled_qty": 2000,
      "settled_qty": 2000,
      "busted_qty": 0,
      "delta_ppm": 0,
      "last_event_seq": 12350
    }
  ]
}

Notes:

  • Orders are ordered most-recent-first by last_event_seq (i.e. by the seq of the last persisted history event for the order).
  • next_cursor is omitted when there are no more rows; pass it back verbatim in the next request to page older.
  • A cursor preserves the first page's event-sequence snapshot and creation-time bounds. Events persisted after that snapshot are excluded from later pages and appear when pagination is restarted without a cursor.
  • Pagination is by distinct order. The page selects orders by last_event_seq and returns one flat row per order.
  • status is one of open, filled, canceled, rejected.
  • side is BID for buys and ASK for sells, matching working_orders and Fill events.
  • price, original_qty, remaining_qty, filled_qty, settled_qty, and busted_qty are raw integers interpreted using the market's symbology metadata, identical to other private/account events.
  • filled_qty, settled_qty, and busted_qty are aggregated from persisted fill/settlement events for the order.
  • event_reason_code and reject_reason_code on the top-level order mirror the latest terminal reason when available.
  • Activated TP/SL legs include conditional_group_external_order_id and conditional_leg (1 = take profit, 2 = stop loss).
  • Detailed lifecycle events are fetched separately with get_order_events.

Common rejects:

  • auth_required (no active authenticated WS session)
  • invalid_get_order_history (malformed request payload)
  • invalid_order_history_cursor (cursor is malformed, unsupported, or conflicts with an explicitly supplied creation-time bound)
  • invalid_order_history_created_from (created_from_unix_s is null or not a non-negative integer)
  • invalid_order_history_created_to (created_to_unix_s is null or not a non-negative integer)
  • invalid_order_history_created_range (equal or inverted creation-time bounds)
  • stream_unavailable (the account-history service is unavailable)
  • order_history_unavailable (the order-history request failed)

Rejected ack responses echo request_id when supplied.

docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "get_order_events",
  "request_id": "order-events-1",
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "market_id": 7,
  "cursor": "",
  "limit": 20
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string get_order_events
  • request_id: optional caller-supplied correlation id; echoed back in the response so multiple in-flight pages can be matched up
  • external_order_id: required order id from the private order stream
  • market_id: required market id for the order
  • cursor: optional opaque string from the previous page's next_cursor; empty or omitted returns the newest page
  • limit: optional page size; clamped to 1..100, defaults to 20

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated wallet-bound session (same gating as subscribe_account).
  • Events are returned for the authenticated bound wallet only; the request does not accept a wallet override.
  • external_order_id and market_id must both be greater than 0.
  • Strict JSON: unknown fields are rejected with invalid_get_order_events.

Response (one order_events event per request, then ack accepted):

{
  "type": "order_events",
  "request_id": "order-events-1",
  "external_order_id": 123456,
  "market_id": 7,
  "next_cursor": "12348",
  "events": [
    {
      "event_type": "settled",
      "client_instruction_id": 0,
      "price": 5000050,
      "qty": 2000,
      "fee": -3,
      "settlement_seq": 55,
      "event_unix_ns": 1735689601000000000,
      "stream_seq": 12350
    },
    {
      "event_type": "filled",
      "client_instruction_id": 9001,
      "trade_id": 77,
      "price": 5000050,
      "qty": 2000,
      "remaining_qty": 0,
      "event_unix_ns": 1735689600999000000,
      "stream_seq": 12348
    }
  ]
}

Notes:

  • Events are ordered newest-first by stream_seq.
  • next_cursor is omitted when there are no more rows; pass it back verbatim in the next request to page older.
  • events[].event_type is one of accepted, modified, filled, cancelled, rejected, settled, busted, cancel_rejected, modify_rejected.
  • events[].price is the order price for accepted, the new requested price for modified, the fill/settlement price for filled / settled / busted, and may be omitted for events without a price.
  • events[].qty is the order quantity for accepted, the new requested quantity for modified, the fill/settlement quantity for filled / settled / busted, and the affected quantity for cancel/reject events when available.
  • events[].reason_code is present for rejected/cancelled/reject events when a reason is available.
  • events[].fee is present on settlement-derived events when available. Fill events can omit fee because fees are finalized with settlement events.

Common rejects:

  • auth_required (no active authenticated WS session)
  • invalid_get_order_events (malformed request payload)
  • stream_unavailable (the account-history service is unavailable)
  • order_events_unavailable (the order-events request failed)

Rejected ack responses echo request_id when supplied.

docs.title: user_deposit_address
docs.text:
Request:

{
  "type": "user_deposit_address",
  "subaccount_id": 0,
  "client_unix_ns": 1710000000000000000
}

Fields:

  • type: literal string user_deposit_address
  • subaccount_id: target trading subaccount id (uint64)
  • client_unix_ns: optional client timestamp in Unix nanoseconds; gateway receive time is used if omitted or zero

Rules:

  • Requires an authenticated wallet-bound session.
  • The wallet is the authenticated bound wallet. The request does not accept a wallet override.
  • The request does not include amount, token account, deposit address, transaction bytes, or VAA bytes.
  • This request registers the derived EVM deposit address for the authenticated wallet and subaccount. It does not transfer collateral or specify an amount.
  • The actual deposit amount is determined from the later EVM token transfer.
  • Send this command before transferring tokens. If a completed EVM transfer is delayed in reaching the trading account, it is safe to send the same request again and wait for another UserDepositAddressStatus.

UserDeposit address derivation:

  • wallet: the authenticated bound wallet as 32 bytes.
  • subaccount_id: uint64, encoded big-endian for the CREATE2 salt input.
  • evm_vault: deployed EVMVault address from GET /v1/evm/addresses field gateway.
  • userDepositInitCodeHash: keccak256(type(UserDeposit).creationCode), exposed on-chain as EVMVault.userDepositInitCodeHash() and returned by GET /v1/evm/addresses field user_deposit_init_code_hash.

Formula:

salt = keccak256(wallet || uint64_be(subaccount_id))
user_deposit_address = last20bytes(
  keccak256(0xff || evm_vault || salt || userDepositInitCodeHash)
)

Clients should fetch GET /v1/evm/addresses from the same gateway they use for WebSocket commands instead of hardcoding local deployment artifacts.

Completion:

  • A successful submission does not emit a generic ack accepted.
  • Wait for the matching UserDepositAddressStatus event. It confirms that the wallet/subaccount deposit address is registered.
  • Validation and forwarding failures still return ack rejected or ack busy.

Busy:

{ "type": "ack", "status": "busy", "reason": "sequencer_unreachable" }

Common rejects:

  • invalid_user_deposit_address
  • subaccount_id_required
  • auth_required
  • invalid_actor_pubkey

docs.title: signed_set_delegate
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_set_delegate", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed set-delegate proof bytes>" }

Raw software-signed proof definition:

  • Wire length: 160 bytes
  • Payload: owner_pubkey(32) || delegate_key(32) || delegate_nonce(8) || request_id64(8) || iat(8) || exp(8)
  • Signature: 64 bytes over the 96-byte payload. Signer is owner_pubkey.

Raw Ledger-signed proof definition:

  • Wire length: 277 bytes
  • Signed payload: 85-byte Solana off-chain V0 prefix || base64(payload96)
  • Signature: 64 bytes over the full signed payload
  • Ledger prefix signer must be owner_pubkey

Rules enforced:

  • Requires owner wallet authentication. Delegate-authenticated sessions are rejected.
  • owner_pubkey must match the authenticated wallet.
  • delegate_nonce must be greater than 0; on-chain validation requires it to be exactly the next user delegate nonce.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use and must be clear.
  • iat and exp must be greater than 0; gateway caps effective lifetime to 5 seconds for raw software proofs and 60 seconds for Ledger proofs.
  • On-chain validation requires iat <= exp and exp not to be expired at execution time.
  • Settlement emits SetDelegateStatus after the on-chain transaction reaches terminal status.

Authoritative result events arrive through the private/account stream.

SetDelegateStatus is emitted for terminal settlement status:

{
  "type": "SetDelegateStatus",
  "seq": 123,
  "client_instruction_id": 9006,
  "wallet": "<owner wallet>",
  "delegate_pubkey": "<delegate pubkey>",
  "delegate_nonce": 1,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "term": 77
}
  • status=0 and error_code=0 means finalized success.
  • Nonzero status or nonzero error_code means settlement failed.
  • Known nonzero error_code values may include error_domain, error, and error_message when available.
  • status and error_code are always present, including zero-valued success fields.
  • Only terminal settlement statuses are delivered as private events.

CreateVault is emitted for non-approved create-vault decisions:

{
  "type": "CreateVault",
  "seq": 122,
  "client_instruction_id": 9006,
  "subaccount_id": 1,
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "source_subaccount_pubkey": "<source subaccount PDA>",
  "operation_subaccount_id": 1,
  "operation_subaccount_pubkey": "<operation subaccount PDA>",
  "vault_id": 0,
  "vault_account_pubkey": "<vault PDA>",
  "participant_account_pubkey": "<participant PDA>",
  "requested_vault_collateral": 1000000,
  "vault_creation_fee": 100000000,
  "total_debit": 101000000,
  "status": 1,
  "error_code": 0,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 77
}
  • status=1 and error_code=0 means the vault already exists.
  • Other non-approved decisions are failures.
  • status and error_code are always present, including zero-valued fields.
  • vault_id is always present; 0 is a valid vault id.
  • Approved decisions are not forwarded as CreateVault; clients wait for CreateVaultStatus.

docs.title: signed_order
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_order", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed order proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_order
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed order proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 191 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_ORDER_V1
  • The raw proof is not JSON. It contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • order ContractOrderV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractOrderV1 fields:

  • symbol uint32
  • price uint64
  • qty uint64
  • tif uint8
  • order_type uint8
  • execution_mode uint8
  • role uint8
  • delta_ppm int32
  • side uint8
  • request_id64 uint64

Allowed enum values:

  • tif: 0 = IOC, 1 = GTC
  • order_type: 0 = LIMIT, 1 = MARK_TO_MID, 2 = MARKET
  • execution_mode: 0 = NORMAL, 1 = MAINTENANCE_LIQUIDATION, 2 = ADL, 3 = VAULT_LIQUIDATION
  • role: 0 = MAKER, 1 = TAKER
  • side: 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL

These enum values are the public signed-wire values.

Role-based command timing:

  • Taker orders become eligible to enter an auction after 300 ms.
  • Maker orders are eligible for the next auction.
  • The same role-based timing applies to cancels and modifies. Maker cancels and maker modifies are eligible for the next auction; taker cancels and taker modifies become eligible after 300 ms.
  • The cancel/modify role must match the live order role, so a taker cannot bypass this timing by marking a command as maker.

Price and quantity encoding:

  • price is a raw uint64 integer carried in wire format; the market's px_exponent is applied to interpret it as a decimal price.
  • Human price is price * 10^(px_exponent).
  • Example: if px_exponent = -2 and price = 10001, the human price is 100.01.
  • qty is a raw uint64 integer carried in wire format in units of 10^(-size_decimals) for that market.
  • Human quantity is qty * 10^(-size_decimals).
  • To encode a human decimal quantity, clients compute raw_qty = human_qty * 10^(size_decimals).
  • A human decimal quantity is valid only if it is exactly representable at that market resolution and raw_qty > 0.
  • This means a client decimal input may have at most size_decimals fractional digits.
  • Examples:
  • BTC with size_decimals = 5: minimum increment is 0.00001; 10.12345 is valid and encodes as 1012345; 10.123456 is invalid because it is not exactly representable as uint64 qty
  • ETH with size_decimals = 4: minimum increment is 0.0001; 10.1234 is valid and encodes as 101234; 10.12345 is invalid because it is not exactly representable as uint64 qty

Limit-price acceptance rule:

  • The gateway validates the price field only for LIMIT orders.
  • The rule is based on 6 - size_decimals.
  • Starting from the scaled decimal price, trailing zeros are stripped first.
  • After stripping trailing zeros:
  • remaining decimal places must be <= 6 - size_decimals
  • if any decimal places remain, the normalized price must have at most 5 significant figures
  • Clients must apply this rule before submitting an order.

Equivalent intuition:

  • More size_decimals leaves fewer decimal places available for price.
  • When decimal places remain, prices are limited to 5 significant figures after normalization.

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • symbol must be active symbology and fit in uint32
  • qty must be > 0
  • For signed raw integer orders, representable quantity precision is implied by the wire encoding above; clients accepting human decimal qty input must reject values with more than size_decimals fractional digits
  • execution_mode must be 0 = NORMAL for gateway-submitted signed orders
  • role must be explicitly provided as MAKER or TAKER; gateway does not infer it from order_type or tif
  • LIMIT orders require price > 0
  • LIMIT orders require the raw price to satisfy the gateway's accepted price grid for that symbol (px_exponent, size_decimals, 6 - size_decimals, 5-significant-figure rule)
  • MARK_TO_MID orders require delta_ppm != 0
  • MARK_TO_MID orders do not use the price field for gateway validation
  • MARK_TO_MID orders require a current mark price in gateway for precheck; the final executable limit is determined at auction time from Pyth
  • MARK_TO_MID orders require abs(delta_ppm) <= 50000, i.e. at most 5% from mark
  • MARKET orders require tif = IOC and role = TAKER
  • MARKET orders may use price as a reference price and positive delta_ppm as the maximum adverse slippage
  • MARKET orders with price = 0 require delta_ppm = 0; this 0/0 combination is an unrestricted market order
  • MARKET orders with price > 0 are protected market orders and require delta_ppm > 0
  • protected MARKET orders require delta_ppm <= 1000000, i.e. at most 100% adverse slippage
  • MARKET orders require delta_ppm >= 0; zero is valid only for the unrestricted price = 0, delta_ppm = 0 combination
  • exp must be > 0. The effective expiry is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.
  • iat is the client send time. Unix-second values are accepted and normalized to nanoseconds for timing fields.

Mark-to-mid price semantics:

  • For MARK_TO_MID, clients should treat price as ignored and usually send 0.
  • The gateway does not apply the LIMIT price-grid rule to MARK_TO_MID.
  • The executable limit is determined at auction time from the current Pyth mark and delta_ppm.
  • delta_ppm is parts per million of that auction-time mark price.
  • The raw price delta is floor(mark_price * abs(delta_ppm) / 1_000_000), with a minimum of one raw price unit for nonzero delta_ppm.
  • Effective limit derivation:
  • buy: derived_limit = mark_price - raw_delta when delta_ppm > 0, and mark_price + raw_delta when delta_ppm < 0
  • sell: derived_limit = mark_price + raw_delta when delta_ppm > 0, and mark_price - raw_delta when delta_ppm < 0
  • Positive delta_ppm moves buys below mark and sells above mark.
  • Negative delta_ppm moves the raw derived buy above mark and the raw derived sell below mark.
  • The derived limit is snapped to the market price grid without worsening the owner price: buys snap down and sells snap up. A small negative delta may therefore snap back to the current grid level instead of crossing.
  • The symbol's explicit limit-price grid affects LIMIT orders directly, while MARK_TO_MID is governed by mark availability, delta_ppm, the accepted delta cap, and price-grid snapping.

Market-order slippage semantics:

  • For a protected MARKET order, price is the client-supplied reference price and delta_ppm is parts per million of that reference price.
  • The raw adverse-price allowance is floor(price * delta_ppm / 1_000_000).
  • A protected buy may execute at or below price + allowance.
  • A protected sell may execute at or above max(price - allowance, 0).
  • Prices farther in the favorable direction remain eligible; the protection is one-sided.
  • Eligibility is evaluated against the auction fill price. The reference price is not added as a clearing-price candidate.
  • The reference price and slippage are used unchanged, without applying the LIMIT price-grid rule to them.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "subaccount_id": 7,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "order": {
    "symbol": 7,
    "price": 5000000,
    "qty": 1000,
    "tif": 1,
    "order_type": 0,
    "execution_mode": 0,
    "role": 0,
    "delta_ppm": 0,
    "side": 0,
    "request_id64": 9001
  }
}

Example meanings:

  • Limit maker buy order: order_type=0, role=0, side=0, tif=1, price>0
  • Mark-to-mid taker buy below mark: order_type=1, role=1, side=0, delta_ppm>0
  • Mark-to-mid maker buy above mark: order_type=1, role=0, side=0, delta_ppm<0
  • Unrestricted market taker sell: order_type=2, role=1, side=1, tif=0, price=0, delta_ppm=0
  • Protected market taker buy with 1% adverse slippage: order_type=2, role=1, side=0, tif=0, price>0, delta_ppm=10000

docs.title: signed_modify
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_modify", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed modify proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_modify
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed modify proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 215 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_MODIFY_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • modify ContractModifyV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractModifyV1 fields:

  • external_order_id uint64
  • request_id64 uint64
  • original_iat uint64
  • original_request_id64 uint64
  • symbol uint32
  • role uint8
  • side uint8
  • tif uint8
  • order_type uint8
  • execution_mode uint8
  • price uint64
  • qty uint64
  • delta_ppm int32

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • external_order_id must be > 0
  • original_iat must be > 0
  • top-level modify iat must not be earlier than original_iat
  • original_request_id64 must be > 0 and must leave bit 63 clear
  • qty must be > 0
  • symbol must be active symbology
  • role must be 0 = MAKER or 1 = TAKER
  • side, tif, order_type, and execution_mode must be valid enum values
  • exp must be > 0. The effective expiry is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Execution rules:

  • The target order must exist and still be live.
  • The target order must not be IOC or MARKET.
  • The modify role must match the original order role.
  • The modify side, tif, and order_type must match the original order.
  • The modify original_iat and original_request_id64 must match the original live order's signed order proof identity.
  • The modify qty must be <= the target order's current live remaining quantity. Modify can reduce or keep size unchanged, but cannot increase size. To increase size, cancel the existing order and submit a new order after the cancel is acknowledged.
  • Only price, qty, and delta_ppm are changed.
  • Maker modifies are eligible for the next auction.
  • Taker modifies become eligible to enter an auction after 300 ms.
  • The role must match the live order, so a taker cannot bypass this timing by marking a modify as maker.
  • MARK_TO_MID modifies use an executable price determined at auction time from the current Pyth mark and requested delta_ppm; invalid derived prices are rejected.

  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",

  }
}

docs.title: signed_conditional_group
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_conditional_group", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed conditional-group proof bytes>" }

The proof is 219 bytes and uses signature domain AETHEON_COND_V1. Its envelope contains the sender, partition, subaccount, iat, exp, the 65-byte conditional group, signer, and signature.

Conditional group fields:

  • symbol uint32
  • qty uint64
  • exit_side uint8: 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL
  • arm_mode uint8: must be 0 = immediate position
  • leg_flags uint8: bit 1 = take profit, bit 2 = stop loss
  • tp_trigger_sources and sl_trigger_sources uint8: bit 1 = oracle, bit 2 = auction; sources may be combined
  • reserved0 and reserved1 uint64: must both be zero
  • tp_trigger_price, tp_limit_price, and sl_trigger_price uint64
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by the gateway and Risk View:

  • At least one conditional leg is enabled and qty is nonzero.
  • Enabled trigger prices must lie on the market price grid; disabled leg fields must be zero.
  • For a sell exit, stop loss must be below take profit. The comparison is reversed for a buy exit.
  • A take-profit limit must equal its trigger.
  • The group must close the entire existing position in the correct direction.
  • The symbol must not have open or pending regular orders.
  • exp is required and may be at most 90 days after gateway admission.

Take-profit legs become GTC limit orders. Stop-loss legs become market IOC orders. The group and each enabled leg receive distinct external order IDs. Conditional groups are immutable; cancel and replace a group to change it.

docs.title: signed_withdraw
docs.text:

{ "type": "signed_withdraw", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed withdraw proof bytes>" }

  • The compact withdraw payload contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • withdraw ContractWithdrawV1
  • Software proof appends signer_pubkey [32]byte and signature [64]byte.

Decoded ContractWithdrawV1 fields:

  • amount uint64
  • owner_wallet [32]byte

  • request_id64 uint64

  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.

{

  "subaccount_id": 7,

  "exp": 1710000005,

    "owner_wallet": "<32-byte wallet pubkey bytes>",
    "dest_token_account": "<bytes32 EVM address word>",
    "request_id64": 9004
  }
}

Withdraw destination policy:

  • dest_token_account must encode the target EVM recipient as 0x000000000000000000000000<20-byte address>.
  • Settlement transfers collateral asynchronously to the target EVM recipient.

DepositVaultStatus additionally reports settlement accounting fields:

  • deposit_amount: requested source debit amount.
  • insurance_payback: amount used to repay owe_to_insurance on the vault operation subaccount before vault credit.
  • actual_deposit: amount actually credited to the vault operation subaccount and used for share/cost-basis accounting.

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • Requires active wallet-bound authentication.
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Authenticated actor must have access to source_subaccount_id.
  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • deposit_amount must be > 0
  • exp must be > 0. The effective expiry is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "deposit_vault": {
    "vault_account_pubkey": "<32-byte vault PDA>",
    "deposit_amount": 1000000,
    "request_id64": 9007
  }
}

docs.title: signed_withdraw_vault
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_withdraw_vault", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed withdraw-vault proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_withdraw_vault
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed withdraw-vault proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 202 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_WITHDRAW_VAULT_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • destination_subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • withdraw_vault ContractWithdrawVaultV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractWithdrawVaultV1 fields:

  • vault_account_pubkey [32]byte
  • vault_shares uint64
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • Requires active wallet-bound authentication.
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Authenticated actor must have access to destination_subaccount_id.
  • request_id64 is passed through unchanged. It is client-defined metadata and may be a nonce, sequence number, trace ID, 0, or otherwise unused.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • destination_subaccount_id may be 0 and must refer to an existing collateral subaccount owned by the sender.
  • vault_shares must be > 0
  • exp must be > 0. The effective expiry is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "destination_subaccount_id": 1,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "withdraw_vault": {
    "vault_account_pubkey": "<32-byte vault PDA>",
    "vault_shares": 500000,
    "request_id64": 9008
  }
}

docs.title: signed_transfer_subaccount
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "signed_transfer_subaccount", "msg_b64": "<base64 signed transfer-subaccount proof bytes>" }

Envelope fields:

  • type: literal string signed_transfer_subaccount
  • msg_b64: base64 of the raw signed transfer-subaccount proof bytes

Raw proof definition:

  • Wire length: 178 bytes
  • Signature domain: AETHEON_TRANSFER_SUBACCOUNT_V1
  • The raw proof contains:
  • sender_pubkey [32]byte
  • partition_id u16
  • source_subaccount_id uint64
  • iat uint64
  • exp uint64
  • transfer_subaccount ContractTransferSubaccountV1
  • signer_pubkey [32]byte
  • signature [64]byte

Decoded ContractTransferSubaccountV1 fields:

  • target_subaccount_id uint64
  • amount uint64
  • request_id64 uint64

Rules enforced by gateway:

  • Requires active wallet-bound authentication.
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Authenticated actor must have access to source_subaccount_id.
  • target_subaccount_id must differ from source_subaccount_id. If the target subaccount does not exist, settlement creates it for the same user.
  • request_id64 must be > 0; it is passed through unchanged and may be a nonce, sequence number, or trace ID.
  • Bit 63 of request_id64 is reserved for system use. Public gateway clients must leave it clear.
  • amount must be > 0
  • exp must be > 0. The effective expiry is the earlier of signed exp and iat + 5 seconds. The signed proof bytes are not mutated.

Decoded proof example:

{
  "sender_pubkey": "<32-byte user wallet pubkey bytes>",
  "signer_pubkey": "<32-byte ed25519 pubkey bytes that signed the proof>",
  "partition_id": "0x01",
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "iat": 1710000000,
  "exp": 1710000005,
  "transfer_subaccount": {
    "target_subaccount_id": 2,
    "amount": 1000000,
    "request_id64": 9009
  }
}

TransferSubaccountStatus is emitted after settlement status:

{
  "type": "TransferSubaccountStatus",
  "seq": 12346,
  "wallet": [1, 2, 3, 4],
  "client_instruction_id": 9009,
  "source_subaccount_id": 0,
  "source_subaccount_pubkey": "<source subaccount PDA>",
  "target_subaccount_id": 2,
  "target_subaccount_pubkey": "<target subaccount PDA>",
  "transfer_amount": 1000000,
  "insurance_payback": 0,
  "status": 0,
  "error_code": 0,
  "batch_id": 44,
  "term": 2
}

Signed submit rules:

  • Type-driven parse/validation (signed_order uses order parser, signed_create_vault uses create-vault parser, etc.).
  • Sender in proof is the user wallet. signer_pubkey must match the authenticated session signer: wallet for wallet auth, delegate key for delegate auth.
  • Client must already be authenticated and wallet-bound.
  • Signed submit never emits auth challenge; unauthenticated submit is rejected.
  • Delegate rules are enforced based on auth mode and delegate binding validity.
  • The public WebSocket API does not expose a signed_deposit command. User collateral deposits use user_deposit_address plus the EVM deposit flow.

Signed submit responses:

  • Successful submit does not emit an immediate acceptance receipt.
  • Authoritative order/cancel/modify/conditional/collateral/liquidation/vault/transfer state changes arrive through private/account stream events such as OrderAccepted, ConditionalApproved, OrderReject, CancelAck, CancelReject, ModifyAck, ModifyReject, UserDepositAddressStatus, UserCollateralUpdate, AccountFundingUpdate, LiquidationTriggered, LiquidationCleared, WithdrawStatus, CreateVaultStatus, CreateVault, DepositVaultStatus, DepositVault, WithdrawVaultStatus, WithdrawVault, VaultOperationSubaccountCollateralChange, TransferSubaccountStatus, and SetDelegateStatus.
  • Local validation and submit transport failures still return ack with rejected or busy:
{
  "type": "ack",
  "status": "rejected",
  "reason": "invalid_symbol",
  "client_instruction_id": 123
}

or

{
  "type": "ack",
  "status": "busy",
  "reason": "sequencer_unreachable",
  "client_instruction_id": 123
}

docs.title: ping
docs.text:
Request:

{ "type": "ping", "client_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000 }

Fields:

  • type: literal string ping
  • client_unix_ns: required integer timestamp supplied by the client.
  • No other request fields are accepted.

Success:

{ "type": "pong", "client_unix_ns": 1735689600000000000 }

RTT usage:

  • The gateway echoes client_unix_ns unchanged.
  • The client should capture a local timestamp immediately before send and another local timestamp when the pong is received.
  • A simple RTT estimate is client_recv_unix_ns - pong.client_unix_ns.
  • This measures application-layer round-trip time from the client clock domain. It does not measure one-way client->gateway latency.
  • The gateway does not provide a server timestamp for RTT calculation because that would mix clock domains and be sensitive to clock drift.

docs.title: Flow A: wallet direct signing (no delegate)
docs.text:
1. auth_wallet with wallet_pubkey + expiry_seconds.
  2. Receive auth_challenge.
  3. Sign challenge and send auth_response.
  4. Before transferring EVM deposit tokens, send user_deposit_address and wait for the matching UserDepositAddressStatus so the wallet/subaccount EVM deposit address is registered.
  5. Transfer collateral to that address, then wait for UserCollateralUpdate before treating the trading subaccount as funded.
  6. Send signed_order / signed_cancel / signed_modify / signed_conditional_group / signed_conditional_cancel / signed_withdraw / signed_create_vault / signed_deposit_vault / signed_withdraw_vault / signed_transfer_subaccount.

docs.text:
Routing:

  • invalid_json
  • unknown_type
  • text_command_too_large
  • binary_message_not_supported
  • invalid_ping

Invalid command payload (unknown/extra fields or wrong shape):

  • invalid_auth_wallet
  • invalid_auth_response
  • invalid_subscribe
  • invalid_subscribe_market
  • invalid_user_deposit_address
  • subaccount_id_required

  • auth_wallet_expiry_seconds_required

  • auth_challenge_required
  • auth_challenge_expired
  • auth_challenge_replayed

docs.title: Funding Accounts
docs.text:
A Superluminal account is identified by a Fogo Ed25519 wallet. Collateral is credited to a numbered trading subaccount after an EVM deposit is observed and settled on Fogo.

The Fogo wallet and the EVM wallet have different roles:

  • The Fogo wallet authenticates the Superluminal account and selects the trading subaccount.
  • The EVM wallet sends collateral and pays EVM gas for manual deposits. It does not need to have the same address or private key as the Fogo wallet.

Never send collateral until Superluminal has confirmed that the derived deposit address is registered.

docs.title: Keypair format
docs.text:
The utilities accept a Solana-format Ed25519 keypair JSON file: a JSON array of 64 byte values. This is also the format produced by solana-keygen.

Protect the file as a private key. The utilities load it locally and use it only to sign the WebSocket authentication challenge; the private key is never sent to Superluminal.

docs.title: Install the funding utilities
docs.text:
The C++ and Python client bundles include cross-platform source utilities under funding-tools. They run with Bun on Linux, macOS, and Windows; no prebuilt executable is distributed.

Requirements:

  • a supplied C++ or Python client bundle;
  • Bun 1.3.14 or newer; and
  • an existing Fogo keypair JSON file.

Install runtime dependencies once from the bundle's funding-tools directory:

cd funding-tools
bun install --production --frozen-lockfile

docs.title: Fund with the public testnet faucet
docs.text:
From the bundle's funding-tools directory:

bun run fund:testnet --keypair /path/to/wallet.json

The command:

  1. authenticates the Fogo wallet through wss://testnet.slx.fi/ws;
  2. subscribes to trading subaccount 0;
  3. sends user_deposit_address and waits for UserDepositAddressStatus;
  4. derives the Arbitrum Sepolia deposit address;
  5. requests testnet USDC from the public faucet; and
  6. waits for UserCollateralUpdate to confirm that the trading balance increased.

Successful output has this form:

Fogo account:        <base58 wallet address>
Subaccount:          0
EVM deposit address: <0x deposit address>
Faucet transaction:  <0x transaction hash>
Trading balance:     10,000 USDC
Funding complete.

Funding complete. confirms settlement into the trading account, not merely submission of an EVM transaction.

The faucet funds subaccount 0 only. It currently mints 10,000 testnet USDC when settled collateral plus pending EVM deposits is below 1,000 USDC. An already-funded account normally receives HTTP 403 until its balance is below that threshold.

Run the utility before starting the C++ or Python client for the same wallet. The funding session would otherwise preempt the client's authenticated session. The utility closes its own session before exiting.

Run bun run fund:testnet --help for endpoint and timeout overrides.

docs.title: Derive an address for a manual deposit
docs.text:
Use deposit:address for production or any manual ERC20 deposit. This command registers the Fogo wallet and subaccount, derives the corresponding EVM destination, and prints the authoritative EVM network and collateral token. It does not request an EVM private key or transfer funds.

bun run deposit:address \
  --keypair /path/to/fogo-wallet.json \
  --gateway https://gateway.example \
  --evm-rpc https://evm-rpc.example \
  --partition-id <u16> \
  --subaccount <u64>

Use the gateway origin, EVM RPC, and partition ID supplied for the same deployment. Successful output has this form:

Fogo account:        <base58 wallet address>
Subaccount:          <subaccount id>
EVM chain ID:        <decimal chain id>
Collateral token:    <0x ERC20 address>
EVM deposit address: <0x deposit address>
Deposit address ready.
Transfer only the listed collateral token on the listed EVM chain.

After Deposit address ready.:

  1. Configure the EVM wallet for the printed chain.
  2. Connect a trading client with the same Fogo wallet and subaccount.
  3. Transfer only the printed collateral token to the printed deposit address.
  4. Observe its account stream and wait for UserCollateralUpdate before treating the trading account as funded.

The address utility exits after registration; it does not need to remain open while the EVM transfer settles.

An EVM receipt proves that the transfer was submitted; it does not prove that the trading balance was credited. Sending on another chain or sending another token will not fund the account.

docs.title: How the deposit address is derived
docs.text:
The deposit address is deterministic for a Fogo wallet and subaccount:

salt = keccak256(fogo_wallet_bytes || uint64_be(subaccount_id))

deposit_address = last20bytes(
  keccak256(0xff || evm_vault || salt || user_deposit_init_code_hash)
)

Inputs:

  • fogo_wallet_bytes: the authenticated 32-byte Ed25519 public key;
  • subaccount_id: the unsigned 64-bit subaccount number, encoded big-endian;
  • evm_vault: the gateway field from GET /v1/evm/addresses; and
  • user_deposit_init_code_hash: the matching field from that response.

Fetch those values from the same HTTP origin used for the WebSocket connection. Do not hardcode deployment addresses.

Before transferring collateral, authenticate the Fogo wallet and send:

{
  "type": "user_deposit_address",
  "subaccount_id": 0
}

Wait for the matching UserDepositAddressStatus. Registration success does not emit a generic ack accepted; validation or forwarding failures emit ack rejected or ack busy.

See user_deposit_address for the full wire contract.

docs.title: Faucet errors
docs.text:
• 400: malformed request, or the deposit address does not belong to the supplied wallet.
  • 403: settled collateral plus pending deposits is at least 1,000 USDC.
  • 502: an EVM or Fogo RPC operation failed.

The public faucet does not require an EVM wallet or EVM gas.

docs.title: Getting Started with the C++ Client
docs.text:
The reference api_client is a C++20 terminal application for connecting to Superluminal, viewing native maker and taker books, monitoring a trading account, and submitting, modifying, and cancelling signed orders.

It is a reference application rather than a complete binding for every public API command. See the public API reference when building a custom integration.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
You need:

  • the supplied C++ client source bundle;
  • a C++20 compiler;
  • Meson and Ninja;
  • pkg-config, OpenSSL, and libsodium; and
  • a Solana-format Ed25519 keypair JSON file for your Fogo wallet.

On Ubuntu or Debian:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y \
  build-essential \
  libssl-dev \
  libsodium-dev \
  meson \
  ninja-build \
  pkg-config

The source bundle vendors FTXUI, IXWebSocket, and simdjson.

docs.title: Build the client
docs.text:
From the root of the standalone C++ source bundle:

meson setup build
meson compile -C build

The executable is written to:

build/api_client/api_client

Confirm the binary before connecting:

./build/api_client/api_client --version

docs.title: Fund the wallet
docs.text:
The bundle includes the source funding utility. Fund subaccount 0 before starting the client:

cd funding-tools
bun install --production --frozen-lockfile
bun run fund:testnet --keypair /path/to/wallet.json
cd ..

Wait for Funding complete.. The funding utility opens an authenticated session, and the public gateway permits one authenticated session per wallet, so running it while the client is connected will preempt the client.

See Funding accounts for keypair requirements, deposit-address derivation, faucet limits, and manual deposits.

docs.title: Start the client
docs.text:
./build/api_client/api_client \
  --ws wss://testnet.slx.fi/ws \
  --keypair ./wallet.json \
  --subaccount_id 0 \
  --partition_id 0x01

Arguments:

  • --ws: WebSocket endpoint; both ws:// and wss:// are supported.
  • --keypair: Fogo wallet keypair JSON file.
  • --subaccount_id: trading subaccount displayed by the application.
  • --partition_id: signed-message partition; public testnet uses 0x01.
  • --feed_ids: optional comma-separated market IDs. When omitted, the client subscribes to every active market returned by /v1/symbology.

The client fetches symbology from the HTTP origin corresponding to --ws, then authenticates the wallet and starts the account and market subscriptions.

docs.title: Connection flow
docs.text:
The client performs these steps automatically:

  1. Fetch GET /v1/symbology.
  2. Send auth_wallet with the wallet public key.
  3. Sign the returned auth_challenge locally.
  4. Send auth_response and wait for ack accepted.
  5. Send subscribe_account.
  6. Request the newest account order-history page.
  7. Subscribe to the selected active markets.

The first private account message is normally AccountSnapshot. Later account messages report accepted orders, rejects, fills, settlements, collateral, funding, modifications, and cancellations.

docs.title: Market data
docs.text:
Native subscribe_market streams contain two book views:

  • bookType: "maker"
  • bookType: "taker"

The client synchronizes them independently and combines them in its ladder. It also consumes Trade events. If it receives stream_reset, it discards the affected local book and resubscribes.

Market IDs and integer scaling are deployment data. Fetch them rather than hardcoding them:

curl --fail https://testnet.slx.fi/v1/symbology

Use px_exponent, tick_size, and size_decimals when converting human prices and quantities to raw wire integers.

docs.title: Submit an order
docs.text:
The order ticket creates and signs a signed_order proof locally. Choose:

  • market;
  • buy or sell;
  • quantity;
  • limit, mark-to-mid, or market order;
  • GTC or IOC where applicable; and
  • explicit MAKER or TAKER role.

Role is not inferred. Market orders require TAKER. For a protected market order, provide a reference price and slippage from 1 to 1,000,000 ppm. Leave both fields empty for an unrestricted market order.

Sending the command successfully is not the final order result. Observe the private account stream:

  • ack rejected or ack busy reports a local command failure;
  • OrderAccepted confirms admission to the account stream;
  • OrderReject reports an asynchronous rejection; and
  • Fill, FillSettled, and FillBusted report execution and settlement.

docs.title: Modify or cancel an order
docs.text: Select a working order in the TUI to modify or cancel it. The client signs the corresponding command and waits for ModifyAck, ModifyReject, CancelAck, or CancelReject on the account stream.

docs.title: First-run checklist
docs.text:
1. Check https://testnet.slx.fi/healthz returns ok.
  2. Fetch /v1/symbology and confirm at least one active market.
  3. Fund the wallet and wait for Funding complete..
  4. Start api_client with the same keypair and subaccount 0.
  5. Confirm AccountSnapshot and market data appear.
  6. Submit a small order and observe its private lifecycle events.
  7. Cancel it if it remains working.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• Session preempted: another connection authenticated the same wallet.
  • Invalid symbol: refresh /v1/symbology and use an active market ID.
  • Invalid price grid: encode the price using current px_exponent and tick_size.
  • Missing balance: complete funding and wait for UserCollateralUpdate before starting the client.
  • Book reset: discard the affected book and resubscribe; the reference client does this automatically.

For complete message schemas and rejection reasons, use the public API reference.

docs.title: Getting Started with the Python Client
docs.text:
The standalone Python SDK includes a Textual terminal application for viewing native maker and taker books, monitoring a trading account, and submitting, modifying, and cancelling signed orders.

It is a reference client rather than a complete binding for every public API command. See the public API reference when building a custom integration.

The SDK is self-contained and installs into its own virtual environment.

docs.title: Modify or cancel an order
docs.text: Select a working order in the TUI to modify or cancel it. The client signs the corresponding command and waits for ModifyAck, ModifyReject, CancelAck, or CancelReject on the account stream.

docs.title: Use the SDK from Python
docs.text:
The reusable pieces live under dfba_client:

  • GatewayClient handles authentication, subscriptions, orders, modifies, cancels, and subaccount transfers.
  • WebSocketTransport owns the reconnecting WebSocket loop.
  • commands contains JSON request encoders.
  • codec validates and decodes gateway messages.
  • signer loads keypairs and creates signed command proofs.

The TUI is an example consumer of these modules. Applications can construct a ClientConfig, initialize GatewayClient, and run WebSocketTransport without using Textual.

docs.title: First-run checklist
docs.text:
1. Check https://testnet.slx.fi/healthz returns ok.
  2. Fetch /v1/symbology and select active market IDs.
  3. Install the SDK with ./scripts/bootstrap_venv.sh.
  4. Fund the wallet and wait for Funding complete..
  5. Start sl-tui with the same keypair and subaccount 0.
  6. Confirm AccountSnapshot and market data appear.
  7. Submit a small order and observe its private lifecycle events.
  8. Cancel it if it remains working.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• Session preempted: another connection authenticated the same wallet.
  • Configured feed missing: refresh /v1/symbology and use active IDs.
  • Invalid price grid: encode the price using current px_exponent and tick_size.
  • Missing balance: complete funding and wait for UserCollateralUpdate before starting the client.
  • Book reset: discard the affected book and resubscribe; the reference client does this automatically.

For complete message schemas and rejection reasons, use the public API reference.
